verdict: Veralto grew sales 7.5% to $1.5B, led by Water Quality, but GAAP operating margin fell as it spent on restructuring and new deals — a one-off tax benefit is what lifted the bottom line.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; core sales +5.1%

segments.name: Water Quality
segments.note: Water testing and treatment — Hach and ChemTreat. Core sales grew 6.4%, led by double-digit growth in water treatment; deals added the rest.

segments.name: Product Quality & Innovation
segments.note: Marking, coding and packaging design and inspection — Videojet and Esko. Core sales grew 3.2% as packaging demand picked up.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running the company — up from $451M a year ago, including restructuring, deal and tax-indemnification items detailed below.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new water and product-quality instruments and software.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $25M; other income was $0M this quarter.
oneTimers: GAAP results include $22M of Cost Optimization Program restructuring costs and $10M of strategic-initiative costs, plus a $39M charge to write down a Danaher-era tax indemnification asset — largely offset in the tax line by a matching $39M reduction of the related tax liability, which is why tax was only $20M on $273M of pre-tax profit.
Adjusted figures also add back $17M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. Adjusted EPS was $1.18 vs $1.03 GAAP, and adjusted operating margin was 25.6% vs 19.7% GAAP.
footerNote: Veralto's fiscal third quarter ended October 2, 2026, the Friday nearest September 30. Segment sales dollars are from the Form 10-Q segment note; the earnings release reports segment growth rates only.

takeaways.title: Water Quality leads
takeaways.text: Water Quality sales rose 9.8% to $939M — core growth of 6.4% plus acquisitions — as industrial customers, including data-center builders, spent more on water treatment and reuse.

takeaways.title: GAAP margin compressed
takeaways.text: Operating margin fell to 19.7% from 23.2% as restructuring, deal costs and a $39M tax-indemnification write-down landed in expenses. The adjusted margin was 25.6%.

takeaways.title: Buying growth, and itself
takeaways.text: Veralto spent $1.1B on four acquisitions and $550M buying back its own shares in the first nine months, and still raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.49–$4.52.

follow100Note: The breakdown rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.
